json.reasoning: The original issue was a SPEC gap: split_fungible_staked_sui_spec had only asserts(split_amount <= original_value) and zero ensures, so result.value == split_amount (and the deduction/conservation/pool_id properties) were unverified -- a wrong-amount implementation (e.g. returning 0) would pass. The current spec adds exactly the contract the triage demanded: ensures(result_value == split_amount) at line 236 (the flagged property), the deduction ensures (value == old - split_amount) at 237, the conservation equality (value + result_value == old) at 241, the original-object pool_id frame at 247, and result_pool_id == old_pool_id at 248. These are substantive postconditions on observable behavior, not a restatement of implementation internals or a cosmetic edit. The two accessors used (fungible_staked_sui_value, fungible_staked_sui_pool_id) carry no_opaque specs and are not include'd here, so they inline to direct field reads, making the value/pool_id comparisons real and provable; this matches the implementation (staking_pool.move:517-537), which sets result.value = split_amount, does value = value - split_amount, and copies pool_id. The fix is purely additive -- the original asserts(split_amount <= original_value) is retained, no ignore_abort or requires was introduced to dodge anything -- so no coverage was weakened and no regression was introduced.

All three checks pass with the green checkmark -- _Check (the 'prover::ensures does not hold' text on splits 3-7 is the obligation LABEL at lines 236/237/241/247/248, each discharged, not a failure), _Assume, and _SpecNoAbortCheck. The originally flagged obligation result_value == split_amount is split 3/7 at line 236 and was discharged. Implementation at sources/staking_pool.move:517-537 constructs FungibleStakedSui { value: split_amount, pool_id: <copied>, .. } after value = value - split_amount, so all five ensures hold. The accessor specs at staking_pool_specs.move:23 and :33 are both no_opaque; the sibling join_fungible_staked_sui_spec (lines 100-114) already uses the same getters in arithmetic ensures within the passing suite, confirming the pattern verifies in this module.
